clinician.final_diagnosis: a presumptive diagnosis of stage IV adenoid cystic carcinoma with metastases to the liver and lung was made
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 29-year-old male presented with right upper quadrant abdominal pain and early satiety. Initial CT revealed hepatomegaly with a 14 cm mass in the left liver lobe. Two months later, a liver biopsy showed a well-differentiated carcinoma with myxoid stroma, tubular and cribriform structures. Concurrently, a chest CT revealed innumerable bilateral pulmonary nodules, favoring metastases. Ten weeks after the initial visit, a CT of the neck identified a 6.5 cm complex bilobed mass in the right parotid gland. A biopsy of this parotid mass showed immunohistochemistry findings suggestive of adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC), though basal cell adenocarcinoma (BCAC) could not be completely excluded without complete removal. Five months later, a CT scan revealed new right frontal hyperdensities, consistent with brain metastasis. Based on these findings, a presumptive diagnosis of stage IV adenoid cystic carcinoma with metastases to the liver and lung (and subsequently brain) was made.
